test_title: PYST 52: SSC MTS 2024 - English Language and Comprehension (Held On: 05 Nov, 2024 - Shift 2)
subject: english
question: Select the option that has an error in the use of present tense.

options.text: The painter is painting the wall right now.
The mother cooks delicious food for her children.
I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour.
I have performed all my duties with utmost sincerity.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence "**I am observing your mischievous activities for half an hour**" contains an error in the use of present continuous tense.
 
• The present continuous tense is used to describe actions happening **right now** or around the current time. However, it should not be used for an action that started in the past and continues for a specific period of time unless it is indicated with a duration or completion.
 
• To express an action that has been happening for a period of time, the **present perfect continuous** tense should be used instead: "**I have been observing your mischievous activities for half an hour**."
 
• Other options are grammatically correct: 
 
 
• **Option 1:** The use of present continuous tense is correct, indicating an action happening right now.
 
• **Option 2:** Simple present tense is correctly used to describe a regular action.
 
• **Option 4:** Present perfect tense is correctly used to describe an action completed in the past with relevance to the present.
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"I **have been observing** your mischievous activities for half an hour."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Present Continuous Tense** is used for actions happening **at this moment** (e.g., "I am eating dinner right now").
 
• **Present Perfect Continuous Tense** is used for actions that began in the past and are still continuing (e.g., "I have been working all day").
